questions.question: Which notation denotes the set of all real numbers?
options: $\mathbb{Q}$
$\mathbb{R}$
$\mathbb{Z}$
$\mathbb{N}$

questions.question: What is the relationship between $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$?
options: $\mathbb{Q}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$
$\mathbb{R}\subseteq\mathbb{Q}$
they are disjoint
$\mathbb{Q}=\mathbb{R}$

questions.question: What does it mean that real numbers complete the rational numbers?
options: They make division by any nonzero number possible for the first time.
They make the rationals dense, so that no two are adjacent.
They add negative numbers so subtraction always works.
They fill limiting gaps left by rationals.

questions.question: Which statement gives the working description of $\mathbb{R}$ used in Math I: Calculus?
options: The complete ordered number system represented by the real line
The dense ordered number system of all fractions with nonzero denominator
The ordered number system of all numbers with a terminating decimal expansion
The ordered system obtained from $\mathbb{Q}$ by adding $\sqrt{2}$, $\mathrm{e}$ and $\pi$

questions.question: Let $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. What does completeness guarantee?
options: The set $E$ has a largest element, which lies in $E$.
The set $E$ has a unique least upper bound in $\mathbb{Q}$.
The set $E$ also has a greatest lower bound in $\mathbb{R}$.
The set $E$ has a unique least upper bound in $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.question: How are the real numbers split by rationality?
options: A real number can be neither rational nor irrational.
Every irrational number is excluded from $\mathbb{R}$.
Every real number is either rational or irrational.
Only rational numbers can be limits of rational sequences.

questions.question: Which statement describes the density of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$?
options: Every nonempty real set bounded above has a least upper bound.
Between any two distinct real numbers lies a rational number.
Every real number can be written as a ratio of integers.
Every real number has a closest rational number other than itself.

questions.question: For $x=10$ and $\varepsilon=0.03$, which positive integer $M$ verifies the Archimedean inequality $M\varepsilon>x$?
What can safely be concluded about $\sqrt{2}$?
options: It is rational because decimal approximations exist.
It is a real number and it is irrational.
It is undefined because no rational squares to $2$.
It is irrational and therefore not a real number.

questions.question: Between any two distinct real numbers, how many rational numbers lie?
options: Infinitely many
Exactly one
Finitely many
None, if both are irrational

questions.question: If $x<y$ and $z>0$ are real numbers, which relation must hold?
options: $xz>yz$
$xz=yz$
$xz<yz$
$x+z>y+z$
